U000001.name: Mo Udall
U000001.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000001.bio: Mo Udall was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Arizona's 2nd congressional district (1961–1991). Udall worked as an educator and businessperson and was a veteran of World War II.

U000002.name: Stewart Udall
U000002.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000002.bio: Stewart Udall was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Arizona's 2nd congressional district (1955–1961). Udall also served as Secretary of the Interior (1961–1969). Udall worked as a lawyer and athlete and was a veteran of World War II.

U000003.name: Daniel Udree
U000003.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000003.bio: Daniel Udree was a Democratic-Republican U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 7th congressional district (1813–1815, 1820–1821, 1822–1825).

U000004.name: Al Ullman
U000004.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000004.bio: Al Ullman was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Oregon's 2nd congressional district (1957–1981). Ullman served in the U.S. Navy and was a veteran of World War II.

U000005.name: William B. Umstead
U000005.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000005.bio: William B. Umstead was a Democratic politician from North Carolina who served as U.S. Representative (1933–1939), U.S. Senator (1946–1948) and Governor of North Carolina (1953–1954). Umstead worked as a lawyer and educator, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of World War I. Umstead died in office in 1954.

U000006.name: Charles L. Underhill
U000006.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000006.bio: Charles L. Underhill was a Republican U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 9th congressional district (1921–1933). Underhill worked as a businessperson.

U000007.name: Edwin S. Underhill
U000007.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000007.bio: Edwin S. Underhill was a Democratic U.S. Representative from New York (1911–1915).

U000008.name: John Q. Underhill
U000008.photoCredit: Compiled by Mitchell C. Harrison, published by the "New York Tribune" newspaper., Public domain
U000008.bio: John Q. Underhill was a Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 16th congressional district (1899–1901).

U000009.name: Walter Underhill
U000009.bio: Walter Underhill was a Whig U.S. Representative for New York's 4th congressional district (1849–1851).

U000010.name: John William Henderson Underwood
U000010.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000010.bio: John William Henderson Underwood was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th congressional district (1859–1861). Underwood worked as a lawyer and judge.

U000011.name: Joseph R. Underwood
U000011.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000011.bio: Joseph R. Underwood was a Whig politician from Kentucky who served as U.S. Representative (1835–1843) and U.S. Senator (1847–1853). Underwood worked as a lawyer and judge.

U000012.name: Mell G. Underwood
U000012.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000012.bio: Mell G. Underwood was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Ohio's 11th congressional district (1923–1936). Underwood worked as a lawyer and judge.

U000013.name: Oscar Underwood
U000013.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000013.bio: Oscar Underwood was a Democratic politician from Alabama who served as U.S. Representative (1895–1896, 1897–1915) and U.S. Senator (1915–1927). Underwood also served as a party leader in Congress. Underwood worked as a lawyer.

U000014.name: Robert A. Underwood
U000014.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000014.bio: Robert A. Underwood was a Democratic Delegate from Guam (1993–2003).

U000015.name: Thomas R. Underwood
U000015.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000015.bio: Thomas R. Underwood was a Democratic politician from Kentucky who served as U.S. Representative (1949–1951) and U.S. Senator (1951–1952). Underwood worked as a journalist.

U000016.name: Warner Underwood
U000016.photoCredit: Warner_L._Underwood,_Representative_from_Kentucky.jpg: Julian Vannerson derivative work: Acdixon (talk), Public domain
U000016.bio: Warner Underwood was an American (Know Nothing) U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 3rd congressional district (1855–1859). Underwood worked as a lawyer and diplomat.

U000017.name: Jolene Unsoeld
U000017.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000017.bio: Jolene Unsoeld was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Washington's 3rd congressional district (1989–1995).

U000018.name: Jonathan T. Updegraff
U000018.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000018.bio: Jonathan T. Updegraff was a Republican U.S. Representative from Ohio (1879–1882). Updegraff worked as a physician, served in the U.S. Army and was a veteran of the Civil War. Updegraff died in office in 1882.

U000019.name: Thomas Updegraff
U000019.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000019.bio: Thomas Updegraff was a Republican U.S. Representative from Iowa (1879–1883, 1893–1899). Updegraff worked as a lawyer.

U000020.name: Ralph E. Updike
U000020.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000020.bio: Ralph E. Updike was a Republican U.S. Representative for Indiana's 7th congressional district (1925–1929). Updike worked as a lawyer and judge and served in the U.S. Marine Corps.

U000021.name: Charles W. Upham
U000021.bio: Charles W. Upham was a Whig U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 6th congressional district (1853–1855).

U000022.name: George B. Upham
U000022.bio: George B. Upham was a Federalist at-large U.S. Representative from New Hampshire (1801–1803). Upham worked as a lawyer.

U000023.name: Jabez Upham
U000023.bio: Jabez Upham was a Federalist U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 10th congressional district (1807–1810). Upham worked as a lawyer.

U000024.name: Nathaniel Upham
U000024.bio: Nathaniel Upham was a Democratic-Republican at-large U.S. Representative from New Hampshire (1817–1823).

U000025.name: William Upham
U000025.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000025.bio: William Upham was a Whig U.S. Senator from Vermont (1843–1853). Upham worked as a lawyer. Upham died in office in 1853.

U000026.name: William D. Upshaw
U000026.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000026.bio: William D. Upshaw was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th congressional district (1919–1927).

U000027.name: Charles Upson
U000027.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000027.bio: Charles Upson was a Republican U.S. Representative for Michigan's 2nd congressional district (1863–1869). Upson worked as a lawyer and judge.

U000028.name: Christopher C. Upson
U000028.bio: Christopher C. Upson was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 6th congressional district (1879–1883). Upson worked as a lawyer.

U000029.name: William H. Upson
U000029.bio: William H. Upson was a Republican U.S. Representative for Ohio's 18th congressional district (1869–1873). Upson worked as a lawyer and judge.

U000030.name: Charles H. Upton
U000030.bio: Charles H. Upton was a Unionist U.S. Representative for Virginia's 7th congressional district (1861–1863).

U000031.name: Fred Upton
U000031.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000031.bio: Fred Upton was a Republican U.S. Representative from Michigan (1987–2023).

U000032.name: Robert W. Upton
U000032.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000032.bio: Robert W. Upton was a Republican U.S. Senator from New Hampshire (1953–1954). Upton worked as a lawyer and diplomat.

U000033.name: Milton Urner
U000033.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000033.bio: Milton Urner was a Republican U.S. Representative for Maryland's 6th congressional district (1879–1883). Urner worked as a lawyer.

U000034.name: James B. Utt
U000034.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000034.bio: James B. Utt was a Republican U.S. Representative from California (1953–1970). Utt worked as a lawyer. Utt died in office in 1970.

U000035.name: George H. Utter
U000035.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000035.bio: George H. Utter was a Republican politician from Rhode Island who served as Governor of Rhode Island (1905–1907) and U.S. Representative (1911–1912). Utter died in office in 1912.

U000036.name: Hubert Utterback
U000036.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000036.bio: Hubert Utterback was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Iowa's 6th congressional district (1935–1937). Utterback worked as a lawyer and educator.

U000037.name: John G. Utterback
U000037.photoCredit: Biographical Directory of the United States Congress, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000037.bio: John G. Utterback was a Democratic U.S. Representative for Maine's 3rd congressional district (1933–1935).

U000038.name: Mark Udall
U000038.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000038.bio: Mark Udall was a Democratic politician from Colorado who served as U.S. Representative (1999–2009) and U.S. Senator (2009–2015). Udall worked as a businessperson.

U000039.name: Tom Udall
U000039.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000039.bio: Tom Udall was a Democratic politician from New Mexico who served as U.S. Representative (1999–2009) and U.S. Senator (2009–2021). Udall worked as a lawyer and diplomat.

U000040.name: Lauren Underwood
U000040.photoCredit: U.S. Government Publishing Office / unitedstates project, Public domain (U.S. government work)
U000040.bio: Lauren Underwood is a Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 14th congressional district, in office since 2019.
